sections.title: From "can" to "could, if you wanted"
sections.content: You already know *-hat/-het* for "can, may" (*kipróbálhatod*, "you can try it"). Put that same *-hat/-het* onto a conditional-mood verb and you get a much gentler suggestion than either a plain command or even the ordinary conditional: *Kipróbálhatnád ezt a receptet* doesn't mean "you must" or even "you would" — it floats the idea as an option, "you could try this recipe (if you wanted)". This is the single most common way Hungarian softens advice into a suggestion rather than an order.

sections.title: Suggestion vs. command
rows: You could try it. (a gentle suggestion)

items.english: You could talk to him/her about this.

items.spanish: Orvoshoz mehetnél, ha nem múlik el a fejfájás.
items.english: You could go to the doctor if the headache doesn't go away.
You could ask an expert for advice.

sections.content: Build it in two steps: take the verb's *-hat/-het* form you already know (*kipróbál* → *kipróbálhat*), then conjugate that as if it were any ordinary conditional verb (*kipróbálhat* → *kipróbálhatnék*, *kipróbálhatnál*, *kipróbálhatna*...). The *-hat/-het* never changes; only the conditional ending on the end of it does.
